requirements.requirement: Establish an integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (hashes + metadata) suitable for detecting later changes
requirements.summary: A manual baseline was built under /var/lib/file-integrity containing sha256 hashes of all 277 regular files, a sorted 305-entry file/symlink list, and a 377-entry stat-based metadata manifest (type/mode/uid/gid/size/mtime) covering files, directories, and symlinks under /etc. A self-hash manifest.sha256 was added to detect tampering of the baseline itself, and the baseline directory/files were locked to root-only 700/600 permissions. AIDE/tripwire/samhain/integrit were confirmed unavailable in the Alpine repos, justifying the manual approach.

requirements.requirement: Later changes to /etc can be identified (and reported) against the baseline
requirements.summary: A reusable /usr/local/sbin/etc-integrity-check.sh script recomputes hashes, file listing, and metadata and diffs against the baseline, printing CLEAN or CHANGES DETECTED with specifics. A live falsification test (appended line to /etc/motd, added /etc/integrity-test-newfile.txt) was correctly detected and reported (motd FAILED hash check, new file listed as added), demonstrating the reporting mechanism works end-to-end, not just that files exist.

requirements.requirement: Baseline reflects a genuinely clean, current state of /etc (no leftover test artifacts) and self-check passes
requirements.summary: After the falsification test, the test file and motd marker were reverted and confirmed absent, the baseline was regenerated against the confirmed-clean state, and the check script then reported RESULT: CLEAN with exit 0.

overall_summary: The executor established a functioning manual /etc integrity baseline on node1 (hashes, file list, stat metadata, self-hash manifest) after correctly determining AIDE and equivalents were unavailable, proved detection works via a bounded and fully-reverted falsification test, and regenerated a verified-clean final baseline. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly: a pre-restart boot_id and CLEAN check, an acknowledged reboot, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and post-restart verification that the baseline, its self-hash manifest, and the check script all remained intact and CLEAN — consistent with the fixed before/after-executor snapshots. The only blemish is a handful of small /tmp scratch/log files left behind by the check script and reboot command that were never cleaned up.
limitations: Temporary diagnostic files (/tmp/etc-*-now.txt, etc-integrity-hash-*.txt) and /tmp/reboot.log were left on node1 after the task; they are low-risk but represent uncleaned residue.

No systemd/service-level view is available on this Alpine node (failed-services observation is unsupported), so service-state recovery could only be inferred from the integrity-check script's own exit status rather than an OS service manager.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were almost entirely read-only discovery, baseline construction, a bounded/reverted falsification test, and the mandated restart-evidence protocol — all with clear causal ties to the task or to the independent restart protocol. The two failed apk install attempts and BusyBox syntax mismatches (stat --printf, sha256sum --quiet) were troubleshooting of read-only/idempotent nature, not destructive mutations, and were promptly corrected (cmd-f0b77920ba2c4048, cmd-8dc500ce3cab4d6e, cmd-71e8a2f970784859). The test-change injection to /etc/motd and a temp file (cmd-ae7579ef73f744b9) was bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted before the final baseline was generated (confirmed absent in cmd-ce94edf8b97b41c6), so it is not treated as unwanted residue. However, the after-executor snapshot shows five /tmp files left behind that did not exist before-prepare: etc-filelist-now.txt, etc-integrity-hash-errors.txt, etc-integrity-hash-full.txt, etc-metadata-now.txt (working files written by the check script's own diagnostic redirections during cmd-71e8a2f970784859/cmd-75ffbb26f14a445c/cmd-ae7579ef73f744b9/cmd-ce94edf8b97b41c6/cmd-b657b802ebe3420b) and reboot.log (from cmd-49fef45d95984d25). None are security-sensitive or destructive, but they are unnecessary residue that was never cleaned up.
